title: Sticky Red Eyes

patient.name: Mdm Tan Geok Hua
patient.presenting_complaint: Both eyes red with sticky discharge for 3 days, no pain

history.hpc: Mdm Tan says 'My two eyes red already, got a lot of 'gum' when I wake up, but never pain one.' Both eyes are affected, with watery-sticky discharge. No pain, no light sensitivity, and her vision is normal. A colleague had the same thing last week.
history.pmhx: No eye problems before. No contact lens use.
history.social_hx: Office worker. Shares a desk with a colleague who had red eyes recently.

examination_findings.anterior_segment: Bilateral conjunctival redness with discharge; cornea clear by observation (for doctor to confirm)

investigations.history_and_triage: Take a focused history and apply the red-eye differential: discharge present, no pain, no photophobia, normal vision and normal pupil point to conjunctivitis.
investigations.red_flags_checked: No pain, no photophobia, no visual loss, not a contact lens wearer — no red flags for a sight-threatening cause.
investigations.triage_category: Routine (Category 4) — minor condition; advise hygiene and book a same-session or routine review per protocol.

diagnosis: History and red-eye differential are consistent with conjunctivitis (marked discharge, no pain or photophobia, normal vision). The PSA recognises there are no red flags, triages it as a minor (Category 4) condition, and gives hygiene advice. No medical diagnosis is made by the PSA.

immediate: Confirm identity and take a focused red-eye history (onset, discharge, pain, photophobia, vision, contact lens use)
Apply the red-eye differential and recognise the conjunctivitis pattern
Confirm there are no red flags (pain, photophobia, vision loss, contact lens use)
Triage as a minor (Category 4) condition and route per clinic protocol
follow_up: Doctor/nurse to confirm and treat as needed
Advise return if pain, light sensitivity or reduced vision develop
patient_education: Explain it is likely a contagious eye infection — wash hands, do not share towels
Avoid rubbing the eyes and do not share eye make-up
Return promptly if vision drops or the eye becomes painful

key_points: Confirms identity and takes a focused red-eye history
Asks about discharge, pain, photophobia and vision
Recognises the conjunctivitis pattern (discharge, no pain, normal vision)
Checks for red flags and finds none
Recognises a likely minor (Category 4) red eye
Does not make a medical diagnosis — routes appropriately
Understands which features would change the urgency
Identifies the infective/contagious nature for advice
Triages as routine and documents clearly
Advises return if red-flag symptoms develop
